Palette, contrast and density per image
Rule-tags plus WHY / AVOID / KEEP notes per image, vocabulary-gated
8 DNA channels with recipes and forbidden moves
4 candidate directions derived from the channels
swiss-case-index-001 and red-monolith-brutal-001 (0 rules in), then swiss-case-index-002 (8 rules in)
Full-page shots at a 1440x1200 and 390x844 viewport
PASS or FAIL per rule for 001 and 002 (new helper, scripts/check-rules.mjs)
Alignment of each page against each lane

commands: mkdir boards/gallery-run && cp boards/demo/*.png boards/demo/profile.json boards/gallery-run/
npm run generate -- --board gallery-run --direction swiss-case-index --model claude-cli:sonnet
npm run generate -- --board gallery-run --direction red-monolith-brutal --model claude-cli:sonnet
# screenshot each page into generated/<slug>/desktop.png + mobile.png
npm run critique -- --board gallery-run --slug swiss-case-index-001 --model claude-cli:sonnet
npm run generate -- --board gallery-run --direction swiss-case-index --model claude-cli:sonnet
limits: One run, one round of critique. The rebuild fixed 3 of 8 rules and broke the mobile layout in new ways (it scrolls sideways at 390px). The loop helps; it does not finish the job.
The pass/fail verdicts come from a vision model reading screenshots. They are a second opinion, not ground truth.
The score measures palette, contrast, density and tags. It can say a page sits in the right lane. It cannot say the page is good.

Every model step ran through the Claude Code CLI on Sonnet (the claude-cli: provider added in this branch), not the repo's default Gemini routing. A different model will give different tags and channels.
The board is 8 synthetic mockups built to span very different styles. A real board should be bigger and more focused than this.
